task: Native archive v2 verify and restore/import

notes: Added crash/fault injection for restore. A fault is injected at each of the six stages that commit canonical state; every one must fail the restore and leave a durable restore_state marker (schema v13) naming the snapshot, so a partial library cannot pass as complete. Adopt/merge/fork refuse to continue into a marked library; replace recovers it and produces a library identical to a clean restore. Three further defects surfaced. (1) An early interruption writes containers and resources before the first document, so LibraryIsEmpty still reported empty and replace - the only recovery intent - was refused, leaving the library with no way forward; a pending marker now counts as non-empty. (2) Container rows used ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING unconditionally, so a restore kept the target's builtin notebooks, search notebooks and default collection instead of the archive's; two restores of one archive therefore differed by their bootstrap timestamps, which also made the packed/loose equality test intermittently flaky. Non-additive restores now upsert; merge still keeps what the target holds. (3) The reader rejected any archive whose source schema was older than the reader, so bumping CurrentSchemaVersion to 13 made every existing archive unreadable including the golden fixture; the ceiling check is removed and the contract documented, since incompatibility belongs in capabilities or the format version. Also closed a TOCTOU window: verification and restore are separate passes over the same files, and note bodies were the one path not re-hashed at use.

notes: Made deduplication symmetric across object layouts. Export checks a hash the store already records (resources.blob_sha256, source_bundle_items.sha256) or that is cheap to compute in memory (note bodies) before opening content, so a duplicate costs an indexed lookup rather than a read and a write; the membership index is the bounded ImportManifest spool, not an in-memory set. Restore's admitted and bundlePaths maps moved to the same spool. Saved 51,876,072 bytes on the packed corpus, within 732 bytes of the predicted duplicate total, and packed export got faster because skipping 52 MB of writes outweighs 215,410 lookups. Two measurements contradicted the reasoning behind the change and drove the final design. The lookup is a net loss on the loose layout, which already deduplicates for free via content-addressed paths: enabling it everywhere cost 7.6% of loose export time to find 27 duplicates, so it is now gated to packed exports and loose export measures back at baseline. And the restore memory saving does not appear under the packed layout at all, where peak RSS is set by reading pack trailers whole; on loose it is a 42% reduction. Also added an integrity check: export now fails if the store's recorded hash disagrees with its own bytes, rather than archiving content under the wrong identity.

notes: Made RecordCounts genuinely optional. This was a bug, not a format trade-off: the field already carried json omitempty, which Go silently ignores on a struct value, so the writer contradicted its own declaration. It affected index entries in both layouts rather than only pack trailers, making it roughly twice the size first reported. Saves 44,159,050 bytes loose and 88,319,535 packed, both within a few kilobytes of prediction. Six struct-typed fields shared the ineffective tag; the four in api/types.go and store.go are always populated, so honouring the tag would delete keys from responses clients already receive and the tags were dropped instead. notes: Schema v14 document_blocks with strictly content-based identity per the user's decision: the hash covers document ID, kind, normalized text, and occurrence among identical blocks, so moving a block keeps its ID and editing its text mints a new one. Line endings and trailing whitespace are normalized first so an editor tidying a file does not break every anchor; document scope means the same sentence in two notes is two blocks, which also stops a block key correlating content across notes. Authored Obsidian ^markers are stored separately and resolve first, since they are names the author chose and survive edits the derived ID does not. Blocks rebuild inside the same transaction as the save, are removed with the document, and RebuildDocumentBlocks fills them in for an upgraded database without writing a revision. GET /api/v1/documents/{id}/blocks returns no block text - it addresses content rather than handing it out. Anchors resolve for notrios:// and document://, with a new stale_anchor status naming the note while reporting the block gone. Folding v13 restore_state into the migration file was necessary: appending v14 there would otherwise have left a fresh database running ensureSchemaV13 after the file set 14, moving user_version backwards. Measured 10k/100k/500k: anchor resolution flat at 0.3ms p95 from 61,200 to 3,001,200 block rows, peak RSS unchanged, and the real cost is disk - blocks roughly double the database at six blocks per note.

Ten read-only checks through notriosctl lint and GET /api/v1/admin/lint/report, with no apply surface anywhere. Findings locate rather than quote - document/resource ID, line, column, reason code, and a SHA-256 of the target - because a broken wikilink's raw text is frequently a private note's title. Every check streams its rows so counts and report_sha256 describe the whole library at any detail cap while memory stays flat; the CLI exits 0 clean and 1 with findings so --quiet works in a hook. Heading anchors are deliberately unchecked: a heading anchor is a slug and block rows store a content hash, so there is nothing to compare against; that needs a stored slug and its own slice. The first implementation ran each check as its own statement and measured 61.3s at 500,000 notes. Per-check timings, added to find that and kept because operators want them, showed six checks each scanning document_links separately - about 10 of the 12 seconds at 100k, with the indexed checks already free. The six link checks now share one ordered scan that classifies each row into whichever checks it violates: 100k 10.9s to 3.2s, 500k 61.3s to 18.9s, every lint test unchanged. Two fixture corrections came from real behaviour: the parser records image embeds as 'embed' not 'image', which had left the alt-text check finding nothing, and CreateDocument substitutes 'Untitled' for a blank title so that state only arises from an importer or interrupted restore.

validation: fresh database bootstraps to schema v15
notes: Schema v15 adds document_blocks.heading_slug with a partial index, closing the gap E2 recorded: a heading anchor is a slug and block rows store a content hash, so there was nothing to compare against. Obsidian's model was verified against its own documentation (headings by text, blocks by ^id, obsidian://open with percent-encoded %23/%5E anchors) and the model is adopted but not the encoding: P5 refuses percent-escapes, so a notrios:// heading anchor is the slug and resolution normalizes heading text to it. Recorded as PROJECT_DECISIONS 19. Two claims in the prompt's sources could not be verified and were not relied on: an Alt/Option 'Copy obsidian URI' menu item and heading=/block= parameters in the Advanced URI plugin. Precedence is author marker, then block ID, then heading slug; repeated headings get numbered suffixes; a heading that slugs to nothing gets no slug rather than an invented one. The unresolved_heading_anchor lint check is restored and runs in Go rather than SQL because matching means slugifying with the parser's Unicode rules; it rides E2's single link scan with a bounded 512-document cache. notriosctl link gained --anchor and --list-anchors and refuses an anchor that does not resolve. A fixture surfaced a real Markdown rule now documented: a space ends an unquoted URL, so the heading-text spelling belongs in a wikilink - independent support for the slug decision. Cost at 100k notes was nothing measurable: lint 3.20s to 3.05s, save 4.17ms to 4.16ms, database unchanged, anchor resolution 0.276 to 0.404ms p95, the last two within run noise and reported as measured.

notriosctl fix repairs the mechanically safe subset of lint findings. Dry run is the default and prints the exact before/after bytes of every edit; --apply repairs one note at a time against the revision its plan was computed from, with per-note outcomes rather than one transaction, and every fix writes an ordinary revision so it is visible in history and revertible. The precondition is not ceremony: the plan's byte offsets describe one specific body, and a span whose bytes are not what the plan recorded is skipped rather than applied at an arbitrary position. non_canonical_link_target runs by default; missing_alt_text is opt-in because a filename is a starting point rather than a description; unlocalized_remote_media is opt-in because it reaches the network and runs the existing localize engine so media policy, SSRF blocking, size/MIME checks and hash rules all apply unchanged. Wikilinks are left alone because rewriting them replaces the author's chosen syntax rather than repairing it. Stale link reference definitions from the plan's list are deliberately not implemented: they are not detected either, since reference definitions are outside the link extractor, so check and fix belong together in a later slice rather than fixing something lint cannot find. A fixture again met the Markdown rule that a space ends an unquoted URL, so [x](Kitchen Plan) truncates - the same rule that decided E1a's slug form, and the fixture now records it.

Fixed a defect E1a left: stablelink.Parse accepted #Kitchen%20Plan and returned an anchor that could never resolve, because validateID refuses percent-escapes but validateAnchor did not. The scheme is now the declaration - percent-escapes are read as escapes only inside a notrios://, document://, or resource:// link, where something declared itself a URI and RFC 3986 already defines %20; a bare Markdown anchor stays literal. This is the user's unique-prefix idea applied to the prefix Notrios already has; a new marker like notrios+q: was considered and rejected because it would not help a pasted Obsidian URI (which carries no Notrios prefix) and would add a second link spelling to the 18 non-test files that interpret a target or anchor. Targets stay literal because a wrong decode there opens the wrong note, while a wrong decode in an anchor lands in the right note and lint reports it. Invalid escapes are left exactly as written and + is not a space; %%20 decodes to '% ', matching urllib, which corrected my first test expectation. Parse still returns the anchor as written so links round-trip byte for byte, and decoding happens at resolution in three places: stable-link resolution, the lint heading check, and backlink counting. Block anchors were deliberately left comparing in SQL since block IDs and markers are letters, digits and dashes and never need escaping. PROJECT_DECISIONS 19 amended: emit slugs; accept percent-encoded anchors inside URI-schemed links only.

notes: POST /api/v1/graph now honours depth. It had been declared in api/openapi.yaml with a minimum, maximum and default and carried through internal/api.GraphRequest into store.GraphRequest since the MVP, while store.Graph never read the field - so every graph slice was the roots' immediate neighbours and a caller asking for three hops had no way to notice. The published node/edge defaults (250/500) also disagreed with the implemented ones (100/200); the implementation adopted the published ones. Added POST /api/v1/graph/path (bidirectional shortest path) and GET /api/v1/graph/report (orphans, isolates, in-degree hubs). No MCP tool and no CLI: MCP profile expansion is v0.6's and this is a client-rendering feature rather than a maintenance one. Three decisions: a bound wider than a ceiling is refused rather than clamped, because clamping is the original defect in another form - a caller who asked for 50,000 nodes and got 5,000 cannot tell a capped graph from a small one; a traversal a ceiling stops reports truncated_by and completed_depth so a partial neighbourhood is never read as complete; and no_path is kept distinct from depth_exhausted and budget_exhausted because only the first proves anything about the library. Expansion is level by level in Go with one bounded IN (...) query per 400-ID batch rather than a recursive CTE, since a recursive walk decides how far it has gone after SQLite has already walked and would bound the result instead of the work; both frontier queries came out as covering index searches. Node metadata is batch-loaded because labelling through getDocumentLocked would have pulled a note body per node. The API response became typed - nodes and edges were []map[string]any, which is how a declared field could go missing without anything noticing. Path search runs from both ends and takes the minimum over every meeting node found at a level, which is optimal for whichever side is expanded. Measured 10k/100k/500k: bounded operations flat across a fifty-fold library (depth-5 18.57 to 19.16 ms p95, path found 2.19 to 2.03 ms), report linear at 0.21/3.92/21.6 s, peak RSS unchanged at 376 MB. Recorded the caveat rather than glossing it: the generated library is a circulant graph whose frontier grows linearly, so traversal timings are a floor and the upper bound comes from the ceilings rather than from this measurement.

notes: GET /api/v1/links/suggest is bounded title autocomplete: a title-prefix index range scan first, then a bounded FTS5 interior-word pass so 'plan' finds 'Kitchen Plan'. A suggestion is an ID, a title, and the canonical URI - never a body, because an autocomplete dropdown is not a place note content should arrive. Two-character minimum: one letter matches so much of a large library that ranking it means reading the library. The second pass is capped at 200 candidates and the consequence is recorded rather than hidden - for a very common word the interior matches shown are the first the index yields, not the best. POST /api/v1/links/check classifies the links in an unsaved buffer and writes nothing. It takes the body rather than a client-extracted target list because deciding what is a link belongs to the canonical extractor; a TypeScript reimplementation would draw markers that disagree with the link records a save writes, and a test asserts check and save agree link for link, status for status, offset for offset. Anchors into the note being edited resolve against the submitted body rather than the saved blocks: while someone types the buffer is the truth about its own headings, and checking a just-typed #new-section against yesterday's rows would mark a correct link broken. Schema v16 adds documents(collection_id, deleted_at, title COLLATE NOCASE, id) and the matching resource filename index, replacing lower(title) = lower(?) which no index can serve - identical semantics since SQLite's lower() folds ASCII only, exactly as NOCASE does. The profile measures its value by dropping and restoring it per tier: indexed suggestion and buffer check are flat at 0.51/1.03/0.44 and 1.40/8.30/1.40 ms p95 across 10k/100k/500k, unindexed they are linear at 41.6/1324/5390 and 19.5/1000/4198 ms - 5.4 seconds per keystroke at 500k, and that cost was already paid by every title-resolved link on every save and every lint pass. One latent defect fixed: resolveLinkCandidateLocked called an anchor-only link resolved even with no source document, producing the ID-less URI document://default/documents/ - unreachable from the save path, reachable the moment a caller could check a never-saved buffer. The web client gained a link picker inserting a canonical URI at the caret and a located list of links that will not open; both debounce, cancel superseded requests, track a generation so a slow reply about older text cannot overwrite a newer result, and degrade to nothing on error rather than to an error banner. E6's input is now a measured fact rather than a preference: md-editor-rt exposes insert at the caret but no caret position and no inline widgets, so broken links are listed beside the text instead of underlined in it; recorded in UI_DESIGN.md and PLAN.md E6.

notes: Recommendation: STAY, recorded as PROJECT_DECISIONS 20. The task's premise was false and finding that out was the task: md-editor-rt 6.5.3 IS CodeMirror 6. It depends on @codemirror/{view,state,autocomplete,commands,language,search} 6.x and exposes them through the completions prop (CompletionSource straight into @codemirror/autocomplete), config({codeMirrorExtensions}), getEditorView() returning the EditorView itself, and domEventHandlers which is CodeMirror's own handler map. So 'migrate to CodeMirror to get source positions and inline widgets' has no content. This forced a correction: E5 recorded that the editor exposes no caret position and no inline widgets, and that claim had reached UI_DESIGN.md, PLAN.md, CODING_CLIENT_HANDOFF.md, PLAN_STATUS.md, FEATURE_MATRIX.md and the archived E5 slice. It came from reading part of the exposed interface (insert, focus) and not the rest (getEditorView, domEventHandlers, getSelectedText). Every document has been corrected; a wrong fact about what a tool can do is worse than an open question, because nobody rechecks a settled one. The prototype had to be real to be evidence and it ran on the editor already shipping, so it was kept rather than discarded: [[ autocomplete inside the editor inserting a canonical link that replaces the trigger, wavy underlines on broken links held in a StateField and mapped through document changes so they follow their text, and Ctrl-click via posAtCoords. No editor was replaced; the migration remains unapproved. web/src/editor-offsets.ts converts the service's UTF-8 byte offsets to CodeMirror's UTF-16 indices - they agree on ASCII and diverge on the first accent, so an unconverted offset underlines the wrong text and further off the deeper into the note; an offset landing inside a character is dropped rather than rounded. applyBrokenLinks refuses when the document no longer equals the body the service classified, the same moved-span rule the publication rewriter and notriosctl fix follow. @codemirror/{autocomplete,state,view} became direct dependencies pinned to the installed versions, verified empirically as one copy each on disk and a byte-identical build, because two copies of @codemirror/state break CodeMirror at runtime. Measured in real headless Chrome on a 206,549-character note, 3 runs per arm: keystroke p50 30.9 -> 30.0 ms, p95 71.4 -> 67.4 ms, eager bundle 259.64 -> 260.94 kB gzip. Stated as 'nothing measurable' rather than 'faster' because first paint alone ranged 160-528 ms across three identical before runs - the within-arm spread exceeds the between-arm difference. What migrating would still buy: dropping @codemirror/language-data, 113 lazy chunks at 1.32 MB raw / 480 kB gzip, 61% of the distribution by size and 97% by file count, for syntax modes a note editor rarely meets; lazily loaded, so distribution size rather than first paint, and not enough against re-implementing preview, sanitizer, toolbar, upload and theming. NOT measured though the task asked for it: behaviour inside the Wails webview - WebKitGTK does not speak the DevTools Protocol the harness uses and no WebKit inspection tooling is installed here; make gui builds and the webview loads the identical bundle so the code path is the one measured, but the engine is not. Also noted: remark-gfm, remark-math, rehype-katex and rehype-sanitize are declared in web/package.json and imported nowhere. New harness scripts/run_editor_profile.sh + scripts/measure_editor.mjs is a CDP client written against Node's built-in WebSocket, so measuring the editor added no dependency.
